entities.summary:
Li Su was a Chinese military officer serving under the warlords Dong Zhuo and Lü Bu during the Eastern Han dynasty of China.

Born into a military family, Li Su rose through the ranks to become a respected general, known for his bravery and strategic prowess. His loyalty to Dong Zhuo was unwavering, but his relationship with Lü Bu was complex, marked by periods of tension and cooperation.

Li Su's significance lies in his role as a key figure in the tumultuous politics of the Eastern Han, where warlords vied for power and the empire teetered on the brink of collapse. His legacy extends beyond his own lifetime, influencing the course of Chinese history and the development of military strategy.

The Li Su legend has endured for centuries, captivating historians and scholars with its intricate web of alliances, rivalries, and power struggles. His story serves as a testament to the enduring power of human ambition and the complexity of warlord politics in ancient China.

Li Su's impact on Chinese history can be seen in the many dynasties that followed, including the Jin and the Han, which both drew upon the lessons of the Eastern Han to navigate their own tumultuous paths to power.
